label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) — Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration

Dana, this is the follow-up I promised after dropping off my own Aria 3. I have now taken the repaired machine through eight days of a civil trial, so this is based on actual work rather than how it felt coming off the bench.

Harbor Point Steno Service is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson. Parking in back is free. I dropped off my Stenvale Aria 3 on Monday, October 19, and picked it up on Tuesday, October 27: six business days against the ten business days quoted. An Aria 2 loaner was issued and returned at pickup.

The work was a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning, and a firmware update from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1. The internal battery was also replaced after Gloria Ruark told me it was holding about 60% of rated capacity. That added $25 to the original $285 estimate, for a total of $310, paid by card at pickup. She asked before adding the battery and said she would not proceed without approval, which matters to me. The work carries a 90-day warranty. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court.

The machine came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from another shop. It is a small thing, but useful to have a proper record of what was done rather than trying to reconstruct it from an invoice.

My first full day back included expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. The recalibration has held up through the eight trial days since, and I am satisfied with Gloria’s work on the machine.

The loaner was less satisfactory. Its tilt arm would not hold its position and slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition. I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria when she emailed about the battery, and she later confirmed that they would repair the arm. I would check that particular unit before taking it out, especially if it will be your only backup.

The phone situation is the real weakness. The line is staffed only Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4. When I called on Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress, it rang out and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria did email the following day, and her emails were clear and responsive, but that does not change the fact that I could neither reach anyone nor leave a message when I called. For anyone working a Monday docket, those hours could be a genuine problem, not just an inconvenience.

Dana, I would trust Harbor Point with my Aria 3 again for the kind of number-bar trouble you described. My confidence is in the bench work: careful repair, prompt turnaround, clear documentation, and no surprise additions to the bill. My reservations are about access and logistics. I would arrange communication by email, not count on reaching them by phone outside those limited hours, and inspect the loaner before leaving. On that basis, yes, I think your Aria would be in good hands.
